confirmed.title: Sign On splash: keyboard focus and screen-reader focus land behind the modal (78 invisible tab stops before the dialog)
confirmed.detail: On first visit the home page opens the Sign On splash (position:fixed, z-index 300, covers everything) but never moves focus into it, never marks the rest of the page inert/aria-hidden, and places the dialog markup at the very end of <body> (after the footer). A keyboard user who presses Tab lands on the (invisible, see separate finding) skip link, then walks through the menubar, toolbar, keyword bar, every window button, buddy list, footer links... all hidden under the teal overlay, before reaching 'Skip sign on' as tab stop 79 of 82. A screen-reader user is likewise not placed in the dialog; aria-modal="true" is set but there is no focus management or focus trap, so Tab wanders through content the sighted user cannot see. Esc works but nothing tells the user that. This blocks or badly confuses non-mouse users at the front door of the store.
confirmed.evidence: Rendered http://127.0.0.1:4301/home.html in the browser pane and queried the DOM: splash open=true, document.activeElement=BODY, main has no aria-hidden/inert, 82 focusable elements, first splash control is tab stop #79. Code: chirpn-windows.js lines 282-367 (`splash.classList.add('is-open')` with no `.focus()`, no trap); theme.liquid lines 58-98 (dialog is the last thing before the toast).
confirmed.fix: When opening the splash: focus the Sign On button (or the dialog container with tabindex=-1), set `inert` (or aria-hidden="true") on <header>, <main>, .tray and <footer> while it is open, and trap Tab inside the dialog; on done() remove inert and move focus to #main or the first window. Alternatively render the splash as a native <dialog> and call showModal(), which gives focus + trap + Esc for free. Same treatment (inert on the page + Tab trap) for the Help Topics dialog (chirpn.js helpShow/helpHide, lines 258-295), which already moves focus but does not trap it.

verdict.reason: Confirmed from source: layout/theme.liquid renders the [data-signon] role=dialog aria-modal=true block after main, tray and footer-group (last thing before the toast), and chirpn-windows.js (~line 286) only does splash.classList.add('is-open') — no .focus(), no inert/aria-hidden on the page, no Tab trap; the only focus() calls in the theme are the Help window ones in chirpn.js:266/271. So on first visit to the home page a keyboard user tabs through the entire hidden desktop (menubar, toolbar, buddy list, footer) before reaching the dialog's controls, and a screen-reader user is left on <body> with aria-modal declared but focus outside the dialog; Esc works but is undocumented. This is a WCAG 2.4.3/2.1.1-level failure at the store's front door, not a retro-style choice, and the fix is small (focus the Sign On button on open, set inert on header/main/.tray/footer while open, or use a native <dialog>.showModal()). Mitigating: only the index template, once per session, and Esc/skip do close it — but non-mouse users have no way to know that, so high stands.

confirmed.title: Every page's og:image / twitter:image URL is 'https:https://...' so shared links get no preview image

verdict.reason: Reproduced. shopify-theme/snippets/meta-tags.liquid lines 52-54 prepend 'https:' whenever og_src lacks 'http' (the protocol-relative CDN URL at Liquid time), and Shopify then rewrites the host to https://chirpn3rd.com/cdn/..., so every one of the 25 mirrored pages (home, products, collections, cart, policies, search, 404, password) emits og:image, og:image:secure_url and twitter:image as "https:https://chirpn3rd.com/cdn/shop/...". confirmed.title: Add-to-cart confirmation and errors are not conveyed to assistive tech (toast is display:none when its text changes; status bar and cart badge have no live region)

Content changes inside a display:none element are not in the accessibility tree, and the region appearing wholesale is generally not announced by screen readers, so `role="status" aria-live="polite"` on the toast does nothing reliable. The status-bar `[data-tip]` cell (flash('Added to cart…')) has no aria-live, and the cart badge update is silent. Net effect: after 'Send It' a screen-reader user hears the button flip 'Sending...'→'Send It' and nothing else; the AJAX error path (`showToast('Error.…')`) is equally silent. Variant price/stock updates ([data-price]/[data-stock]) are also unannounced.

Add `aria-live="polite"` to `[data-price]`/`[data-stock]` on the product page.

The success path (chirpn.js:178-190) gives no other accessible feedback: flash() writes to the footer [data-tip] cell (sections/footer.liquid:35) which has no aria-live, the cart badge update is silent, and the catch path only calls showToast. It does not block purchase (cart page still works), so medium is the right grade; fix by using visibility/opacity/transform hiding, or a permanently rendered visually-hidden live region written on every showToast/flash, with role=alert for the error case.

confirmed.title: Product grid drops to a single 330px column on phones even though card images are sized for 45vw
confirmed.detail: `.grid{grid-template-columns:repeat(auto-fill,minmax(190px,1fr))}` has no phone override, so at 375/390 the Merch Center, collections, search and 'Also In' grids render one card per row with a ~330px square image; roughly 1.5 products fit per screen and 27 products = ~10,000px of scrolling. The card snippet's `sizes: '(max-width: 860px) 45vw, 220px'` shows two columns were intended; because the real slot is ~88vw the browser picks the 600w candidate for a 330px×3 (≈990px) slot on 3x phones, so cards are also soft/blurry.
confirmed.evidence: Rendered tees.html, all.html, search.html, product-tee.html (Also In) at 375 and 390 wide; one card per row, ~380px per card. CSS line 285; snippets/product-card.liquid line 11.
confirmed.fix: Add to the ≤860 block: `.grid{grid-template-columns:repeat(2,minmax(0,1fr));gap:8px}` (keeps cards ≈160px, matches the existing 45vw sizes), and let `.card__name` wrap (see next finding) so two-column names stay readable.

verdict.reason: Reproduced in a real 375px viewport (Chrome, DPR 2): getComputedStyle(.grid).gridTemplateColumns = "329px" (one column), each .card is 329x370px so ~2 products per screen; img.currentSrc resolves to the width=400 candidate for a 323px CSS slot (646 device px), so thumbnails are upscaled/soft. chirpn.css:285 has no override inside the max-width:860 block (lines 503-536), while snippets/product-card.liquid:11 declares sizes '(max-width: 860px) 45vw' — a two-column layout was clearly intended. Not a retro-design choice; it hurts browsing on the main shopper device. Medium is fair: purchase path still works, but catalog browsing on phones is needlessly long and blurry. Suggested fix stands: add `.grid{grid-template-columns:repeat(2,minmax(0,1fr));gap:8px}` to the ≤860 block (and let .card__name wrap). Note: headless Chrome --window-size screenshots do NOT reproduce this (they don't shrink the layout viewport); use a real device emulation viewport.

confirmed.title: 'Returns handled like grown-ups.' under the buy button implies returns exist; the refund policy says there are none for size/change of mind
confirmed.detail: The product small print (default disclaimer setting) reads 'Printed on demand and shipped by Printful. US shipping only for now. Returns handled like grown-ups.' A shopper reads that as 'you can return it'. The live Refund policy says: 'Wrong size or changed your mind — because each item is made just for you, we don't accept returns or offer exchanges for buyer's remorse or sizing.' Only misprints/damage/lost are covered. Putting a vague pro-returns line right where the buying decision happens, contradicted by the policy, is the kind of thing that turns into chargebacks and 'but your site said' emails.
confirmed.evidence: sections/main-product.liquid schema default for 'disclaimer' (line 172), rendered on product-tee.html / product-hat.html / product-ch3rd.html; policy-refund.html mirror text.
confirmed.fix: Change the default to something true and still in voice, e.g. 'Printed on demand, shipped by Printful. US only for now. Made to order, so no size swaps: check the size chart. Misprints replaced free.' and link the words to /policies/refund-policy.

verdict.reason: Reproduced: sections/main-product.liquid:172 default 'Small print' says 'Returns handled like grown-ups.' and it renders on product-tee/hat/ch3rd mirrors, while the live Refund policy mirror says no returns/exchanges for sizing or change of mind (only misprint/damage/lost). Copy at the buy decision implies returns are available; policy contradicts it. Not a legal breach (policy governs) but a real expectation mismatch that invites disputes — medium. Fix: reword default to state made-to-order/no size swaps, misprints replaced, and link to /policies/refund-policy.

confirmed.title: Refund policy tells buyers to 'check the size chart on each product' but no product page has a size chart
confirmed.detail: The refund policy denies sizing returns and says 'Please check the size chart on each product before ordering.' The product template renders only the Shopify description in 'The Details' and there is no size chart/table anywhere in the theme; the tee description just says 'Runs true to size'. Grepping all mirrored pages for 'size chart' / 'size guide' / 'sizing' hits only policy-refund.html. Customers are being told they had the info and didn't use it, when it was never on the site.
confirmed.evidence: grep -il 'size chart|size guide|sizing' over mirror/*.html → only policy-refund.html; sections/main-product.liquid has no size-chart block; product-tee.html 'The Details' text.
confirmed.fix: Add a size chart: simplest is a per-product metafield or a 'Sizing' window on the product template fed from a page/metafield, populated with Printful's size tables for the blanks used (Bella+Canvas 3001, Gildan 5000, etc.). Until it exists, soften the refund-policy sentence to 'message us before you buy if you're between sizes'.

verdict.reason: Reproduced: mirror/policy-refund.html says "no returns for sizing. Please check the size chart on each product before ordering", but grep of all mirrored pages and the whole shopify-theme/ tree finds no size chart, size guide, or measurement table; sections/main-product.liquid (lines ~126-131) renders only product.description in 'The Details', and product-tee / product-ch3rd descriptions contain no chest/length measurements (tee just says "Runs true to size"; only the hat lists head circumference). Denying sizing returns while pointing at nonexistent info is a real customer-trust/dispute problem, not a matter of taste; medium since it does not block checkout. confirmed.title: 'Free sticker in every bag. Every time. No exceptions.' is promised in three places but nothing in the fulfilment setup backs it
confirmed.detail: The Welcome window's 'Garage Deal' says 'Free sticker in every bag. Every time. No exceptions.', the default product pitch on every product says 'free sticker in the bag', and the You've Got Chirp Tee description says 'free sticker in every bag'. Orders are printed and shipped by Printful directly (OPERATIONS.md, shipping policy). Printful only adds pack-ins for warehoused inventory (a paid extra); nothing in OPERATIONS.md, the shipping policy or catalog/polish-plan.json mentions a sticker insert. If it isn't actually configured, this is a concrete promise ('No exceptions') that every single order will break on day one.
confirmed.evidence: templates/index.json line 98; sections/main-product.liquid line 170 default pitch (rendered on all three product mirrors); product-tee.html description; OPERATIONS.md 'Shipping' and 'Adding a product' sections describe Printful pushing/shipping with no insert step; polish-plan.json contains no 'sticker in' copy.
confirmed.fix: Either confirm Printful is set up to include a sticker with every order (and note it in OPERATIONS.md), or cut the claim to something you can keep, e.g. 'Garage Deal: stickers are $5. Buy one, be a nerd.' and remove 'free sticker' from the pitch default and tee description.

verdict.reason: Reproduced. The promise is live in three places: shopify-theme/templates/index.json:98 ("Free sticker in every bag. Every time. No exceptions."), shopify-theme/sections/main-product.liquid:170 default pitch ("free sticker in the bag" — renders on product-tee, product-hat and product-ch3rd mirrors), and the You've Got Chirp Tee description in the mirror ("Printed one at a time, no warehouse, no minimums, free sticker in every bag"). Nothing on disk backs it: OPERATIONS.md only lists stickers as a $5 category and describes Printful print-and-ship with no insert step; polish-plan.json and the shipping policy have no pack-in mention. The tee copy even says "no warehouse", and Printful pack-ins require warehoused inventory, so the claim is internally contradicted. Not a theme bug and I cannot see the Printful account, so it is a verify-or-cut item rather than a confirmed break; medium is right — a "No exceptions" promise that every order may fail is a real trust/refund-request risk at launch, not a taste call.

confirmed.title: One section-wide 'IM pitch' line is stamped on every product, including hats, stickers, phone cases
confirmed.detail: The pitch ('heavyweight blank, print goes hard. free sticker in the bag.') is a section setting, so it renders identically on every product. verdict.reason: Reproduced: sections/main-product.liquid:40-44 renders section.settings.pitch (default at :169-170) on every product; mirrored product-hat.html shows "TheGarage: heavyweight blank, print goes hard. free sticker in the bag." under "Dad Hat" (100% cotton embroidered cap), and product-tee.html's own description says Bella + Canvas 3001 4.2 oz, contradicting "heavyweight". confirmed.title: Merch Center window and page title say 'Products'
confirmed.detail: Every entry point calls /collections/all 'Merch Center' (toolbar, buddy footer, keyword MERCH, Help → 'Straight to the Merch Center', 404, empty states), but the collection template uses collection.title, and Shopify's automatic all-products collection is titled 'Products'. So the window titlebar reads 'Products' and the tab reads 'Products · Chirp'n3rd'. Same for og:title.
confirmed.evidence: all.html mirror: <title>Products · Chirp'n3rd</title>, window title 'Products', og:title 'Products'; main-collection.liquid line 27 renders collection.title.
confirmed.fix: In main-collection.liquid assign a title: `{% if collection.handle == 'all' %}Merch Center{% else %}{{ collection.title }}{% endif %}` and use it for the window; in layout/theme.liquid do the same for doc_title when template.name == 'collection' and collection.handle == 'all'.

verdict.reason: Reproduced in the all.html mirror: window titlebar span reads "Products", <title> is "Products · Chirp'n3rd", og:title "Products", and the min/max/close aria-labels say "Products". Meanwhile 9 places in the theme (header toolbar, buddy rail, Help keyword MERCH, 404, search/collection empty states, featured-merch) send shoppers to "Merch Center". Cause is exactly as stated: sections/main-collection.liquid:27 renders collection.title unmodified and layout/theme.liquid:19-31 builds doc_title from page_title with no all-collection override. Suggested fix (assign a title of "Merch Center" when collection.handle == 'all' in both the section and theme.liquid doc_title) is correct; alternatively rename the automatic collection in Shopify admin, which fixes it with no code. Doesn't block buying, so medium stands rather than high.

confirmed.title: Menubar 'Sign Off' does not sign a logged-in customer off
confirmed.detail: 'My Account' sits next to 'Sign Off' in the menubar. 'Sign Off' only clears sessionStorage and reloads the home page so the Sign On splash plays again (chirpn.js 335-340). A customer who logged in via My Account and clicks Sign Off stays logged in; the real logout is a small 'Sign Off' link inside the account window (main-account.liquid line 7). Two controls with the same label, only one of which does the thing a shopper would expect on a shared computer.
confirmed.evidence: sections/header.liquid lines 8-9; assets/chirpn.js lines 335-340; sections/main-account.liquid line 7.
confirmed.fix: Render `{% if customer %}Sign Off{% else %}{% endif %}`; optionally have the logout link also clear the sessionStorage flag.

verdict.reason: Confirmed in source: sections/header.liquid:9 renders an unconditional <button data-signoff> in the menubar, and assets/chirpn.js:335-339 only removes the sessionStorage 'chirpn3rd-signed-on' flag and redirects to '/'; nothing hits routes.account_logout_url. The only real logout is the small 'Sign Off' link in sections/main-account.liquid:7. So a customer logged into My Account (link right next to it, header.liquid:8) who clicks menubar 'Sign Off' sees the Sign On splash replay but stays authenticated — a genuine shared-computer/privacy hole with two identically labelled controls doing different things. Not a retro-design matter. Medium (not high) because it only affects logged-in account holders and does not block purchasing; suggested fix of `{% if customer %}<a href="{{ routes.account_logout_url }}">` else the splash-reset button is correct and cheap.

confirmed.title: bird-white.png (1600x1163, 357 KB) is downloaded on every page and is the LCP element on desktop
confirmed.detail: The mascot PNG is 1600x1163 px, RGBA, 356,813 bytes (228.8 KB on the wire from the CDN). It is used only at tiny/decorative sizes: the toast icon at 38x28 (theme.liquid:111, inside a display:none .toast, non-lazy so it fetches on EVERY page), the desktop watermark at 420 px / opacity .07 (theme.liquid:49-50; the loading="lazy" there is meaningless because the element is position:fixed and always in-viewport), the buddy-list header at 26x19 (buddy-list.liquid:4), channels rail at 88x64 (channels.liquid:5), 404/cart-empty/list-collections at 88-120 px. Result: it is the single largest asset on every page (229 KB vs. 6.5 KB CSS + 8.6 KB JS + ~20 KB of product images), it becomes the LCP element on home/collection/cart/search on desktop, and on phones (where the watermark is display:none) it is 229 KB of pure waste per page. Decoding it costs ~7.4 MB of bitmap memory for a 26 px icon.
confirmed.evidence: Playwright/CDP network capture of the mirrored pages: tees@1440 = 369 KB total, bird-white.png 229.1 KB, LCP element IMG.desktop__mark; cart-empty@1440 = 325 KB total, 229 KB is bird-white; product-tee@375 (mobile) = 367 KB, bird-white 228.8 KB even though nothing visible uses it. Under Fast-3G throttling bird-white finished at 3063 ms while every other image on the home page finished by ~1200 ms. `sips` on assets/bird-white.png: 1600x1163 hasAlpha. Same PNG re-encoded at 840 px/64 colours = 35 KB, 420 px = 15 KB, 176 px = 5 KB.
confirmed.fix: Ship two small assets: bird-white-840.png (or an SVG of the bird) for the watermark, and a ~176 px bird-white-sm.png for the toast/buddy/channel icons; or upload the mascot to Files and use `image_url: width: N` so the CDN serves resized WebP/AVIF. Additionally put loading="lazy" on the toast (theme.liquid:111) so the hidden toast does not fetch on load, and drop the useless loading="lazy" on the fixed watermark. Expected saving: ~200 KB per page and LCP moves to actual content.

verdict.reason: Reproduced: assets/bird-white.png is 1600x1163 RGBA, 356,813 bytes on disk and 356,861 bytes content-length from the live CDN (uncompressed PNG). It is referenced in layout/theme.liquid:49 (watermark, 420px, opacity .07, position:fixed) and theme.liquid:111 (toast icon 38x28 inside .toast which is display:none — a non-lazy there still fetches on every page), plus buddy-list.liquid:4 (26x19), channels.liquid:5, main-404, main-list-collections, main-cart, main-product. On phones chirpn.css:516 hides .desktop__mark, but the toast/buddy-list references still pull the full 357 KB. So every page ships a ~357 KB decorative asset that dwarfs the CSS+JS and becomes the largest/LCP candidate. However nothing breaks and pages otherwise remain light, so this is a noticeable perf hole (slower first paint on mobile/3G, wasted bandwidth), not a launch-blocker; medium rather than high. Fix as suggested: ship an ~840px watermark PNG/SVG and a ~176px icon PNG (or use Files + image_url width:), add loading="lazy" to the toast img at theme.liquid:111.

confirmed.title: You've Got Pictures loads 1.6 MB on open: 1600 px JPEGs with no srcset, and two neighbours preloaded immediately
confirmed.detail: The stage image is the full 1600 px asset (main-pictures.liquid:21, :34, :48) with no srcset/sizes, so a phone with a 343 px-wide stage downloads the same 1600x1066 file as desktop. `show(0)` runs on load and immediately preloads both neighbours (chirpn.js:231-234), so before the visitor touches anything the browser has fetched pics-01 (337 KB) + pics-02 (447 KB) + pics-11 (303 KB) + 11 thumbs (~200 KB) + the usual chrome = 1,618 KB. Because these live in the theme's assets folder, Shopify's CDN cannot resize them or serve WebP/AVIF (product images from /cdn/shop/files come back as webp/avif; the pics come back as the original JPEG). Browsing all 11 photos costs ~3.2 MB. Every JPEG in the set is 140-457 KB.
confirmed.evidence: CDP network log pictures@1440 and @375: 21 requests, 1618 KB, Image=1576 KB; top three: pics-02.jpg 447.4 KB, pics-01.jpg 337.8 KB, pics-11.jpg 302.8 KB. curl -sI on the CDN URLs: content-type image/jpeg (no webp negotiation) with content-length 369498 / 457218 / 326813. Local re-encode of pics-02 at 900 px q80 = 166 KB, 750 px = 119 KB (vs 457 KB).
confirmed.fix: Either move the photos to Files (Content > Files) or use image blocks (already supported by the section) so `image_url: width:` + `widths`/`sizes` can serve 480/800/1200 renditions as WebP/AVIF; or pre-generate 800 px and 1200 px versions in assets and set srcset/sizes on .pics__img and data-full. In chirpn.js, only warm the *next* image and only after the current one has finished loading (`img.onload` or `requestIdleCallback`), not both neighbours synchronously on `show(0)`. Re-encode the source JPEGs at q~80 progressive.

verdict.reason: Confirmed against the mirrored live page and repo: main-pictures.liquid:21 renders the stage as the 1600px asset with no srcset/sizes; the live page uses the built-in asset set (11 thumbs, data-full = /cdn/shop/t/2/assets/pics-NN.jpg), and curl on that CDN URL with an image/avif,webp Accept header returns content-type image/jpeg, content-length 457218 — so no CDN resizing/format negotiation is possible for theme assets. chirpn.js:220-236 calls show(0) on load, which sets the full 1600px src and synchronously kicks off new Image() preloads for both neighbours (pics-02 and pics-11), so ~1.1 MB of full-size JPEG plus ~200 KB of thumbs is fetched before any interaction, identical on a 375px phone. Asset sizes on disk (140-457 KB each, 11 files) match the claim. This is a secondary gallery page, not the purchase path, so medium is right: noticeable mobile-data/perf cost with an easy fix (image blocks / Files with image_url widths+sizes, or pre-generated 800/1200px renditions with srcset; preload only the next image after the current one loads).

confirmed.title: Home page (and every non-product page) ships with no meta description; home <title> is just the bare brand
confirmed.detail: `<meta name="description">` is only emitted when Shopify's `page_description` is set. It is nil on the home page (no homepage meta description in admin), on every collection (Tees, Posters, All), the Contact and You've Got Pictures pages, cart, search and 404. Meanwhile meta-tags.liquid already computes a sensible fallback (`og_desc` -> shop.description -> 'Apparel for people who drive like it. Have Fun Shift Hard.') but that fallback is only used for og:/twitter:, never for the SEO description. The home <title> is also just 'Chirp'n3rd' — a coined word with no descriptor, so the SERP gives Google nothing but the brand and whatever body text it scrapes (buddy-list screen names, 'yo / u up?' IM lines, Sign On dialog copy).
confirmed.evidence: Mirrored live HTML: home.raw, tees.raw, all.raw, posters-empty.raw, contact.raw, pictures.raw, cart-*.raw, search*.raw, 404.raw all contain zero `<meta name="description"` tags; only product-*.raw have one. home.raw <title> is 'Chirp'n3rd'. og:description on all of these is the hard-coded fallback string, proving shop.description is also empty in admin.
confirmed.fix: In theme.liquid, compute the description with the same fallback chain the OG snippet uses (e.g. move the og_desc logic into theme.liquid or have meta-tags.liquid also output `<meta name="description">`), so every page has one. Then in admin: set the homepage meta title/description (Online Store > Preferences), give each collection a description, and set SEO descriptions on the Contact and Pictures pages. Consider a home title like 'Chirp'n3rd — Have Fun Shift Hard' (brand + tagline) rather than the bare brand.

verdict.reason: Reproduced: shopify-theme/layout/theme.liquid:32 emits <meta name="description"> only when page_description is set; all mirrored non-product pages (home, tees, all, posters-empty, collections, contact, pictures, cart-*, search*, 404, policy-*) contain 0 description tags while product-*.html each have 1. og:description on those pages is the hard-coded 'Apparel for people who drive like it. Have Fun Shift Hard.' fallback from snippets/meta-tags.liquid, confirming shop.description is empty in admin. Home <title> is bare 'Chirp'n3rd'. Real SEO gap for the owner (weak/random SERP snippets, coined-word title with no descriptor) and trivially fixable by reusing the og_desc fallback for the SEO meta + setting admin descriptions, but it does not break the purchase path, legal compliance, or accessibility, and the store is password-gated so nothing is indexed yet — medium, not high.

confirmed.title: No structured data anywhere: products have no Product/Offer JSON-LD, site has no Organization/WebSite schema
confirmed.detail: Shopify's content_for_header does not inject schema.org markup; themes are expected to (Dawn ships Product + Organization/WebSite JSON-LD). This theme has none, so product pages are ineligible for price/availability rich results and Merchant Center free-listing enrichment, and the brand gets no sitelinks-search/logo signals. The theme already computes everything needed for the OG product tags (price, currency, availability, image), so the data is at hand.
confirmed.evidence: `grep -rn 'ld+json\|schema.org' shopify-theme/` returns nothing; product-tee.raw / product-ch3rd.raw / product-hat.raw contain 0 occurrences of 'application/ld+json' (content_for_header only adds shopify-features / analytics JSON).
confirmed.fix: Add a `<script type="application/ld+json">` Product block in main-product.liquid (name, description, image, sku, brand, offers with price/priceCurrency/availability/url, itemCondition) and an Organization + WebSite (with SearchAction pointing at /search?q={search_term_string}) block in theme.liquid for the index template. Optionally BreadcrumbList on product/collection.

verdict.reason: Reproduced: `grep -rn 'ld+json\|schema.org' shopify-theme/` returns nothing and the mirrored product-tee.html / home.html contain 0 `application/ld+json` blocks, so no Product/Offer, Organization or WebSite structured data reaches the page. It does not block buying, but at launch it forfeits price/availability rich results and Merchant Center enrichment on every product page and brand/sitelinks-search signals on the home page. The data is already computed in shopify-theme/snippets/meta-tags.liquid:71-72 (product:price:amount/currency OG tags), so adding a Product JSON-LD block in main-product.liquid and Organization/WebSite JSON-LD in layout/theme.liquid is a small, contained fix. Medium is fair; not high because it is an SEO/discoverability hole rather than a purchase-path or legal defect.

confirmed.title: Collection pages, home, contact, cart, search have no H1 — the window title bar is a bare span
confirmed.detail:

CHIRP'N3RD TODAY

` plus two H2s from the hidden Help window. Product pages and policy pages do have an H1, so this is a per-template gap, not a design choice. This can be fixed without changing a pixel of the Win95 look.

verdict.reason: Reproduced: grep over the mirrored HTML shows tees/all/posters-empty/collections/home/contact/cart-*/search*/pictures/404 have 0 <h1>, while product-*/policy-* have 1; snippets/window.liquid:14 renders the title as a bare <span class="win__title"> and main-collection.liquid:27 passes collection.title only as that title. confirmed.title: CH3RD and Dad Hat expose Printful's supplier boilerplate and cost-plus prices in meta description, OG description and product:price
confirmed.detail: Two of the three mirrored products still carry Printful's default copy: CH3RD's description/og:description reads 'The Gildan 5000 Classic Tee ... Add your design for a long-lasting tee...' and Dad Hat's reads 'Customize it with your embroidery designs and add it to your own collection!'. 'You've Got Chirp Tee' shows the intended state (brand-voice copy, $28.0), so this is per-product cleanup that was skipped, not a theme bug.
confirmed.evidence: product-ch3rd.raw: `<meta name="description" content="The Gildan 5000 Classic Tee ... Add your design for a long-lasting tee that feels timeless and chic. 100% cotton. confirmed.title: Cart quantity auto-submit timer can cancel a Check Out (or Remove) navigation
confirmed.detail: Changing a cart qty schedules `form.submit()` 600 ms later and nothing ever clears that timer. If the shopper edits a quantity and then clicks Check Out (blur fires change → timer armed; click submits the form with name=checkout), the pending programmatic submit fires 600 ms later, cancels the in-flight checkout navigation and replaces it with a plain cart update — the shopper lands back on the cart instead of checkout. Same for the Remove link (GET /cart/change gets cancelled by a POST that re-asserts the old quantities). Only fails to reproduce if Shopify's checkout redirect commits within 600 ms, which is not guaranteed on mobile.
confirmed.evidence: Verified on the mirrored cart-1item page: set qty, dispatch change, click button[name=checkout] → submit event with submitter=checkout at t=1ms, then programmatic form.submit() fired at t=602ms. Timer is never cleared on submit/click anywhere in chirpn.js.
confirmed.fix: On the cart form's submit event (and on .cart__remove clicks) call clearTimeout(qtyTimer). Better: drop the auto-submit and update via fetch('/cart/change.js') with the in-flight/disable pattern used on the product page, or just leave it to the Update Cart button.

verdict.reason: Confirmed in shopify-theme/assets/chirpn.js:204-212 and sections/main-cart.liquid:4-58: the qty input's change handler arms a 600 ms setTimeout that calls form.submit() and nothing clears it on the form's submit event or on .cart__remove clicks (grep shows qtyTimer is only touched inside that one handler). Check Out (name=checkout) and Remove (GET /cart/change) both live in/near the same form, so the realistic flow "bump quantity with the spinner or type it, then immediately click Check Out" leaves a pending programmatic submit; if Shopify's POST /cart -> 302 -> checkout redirect chain hasn't committed within 600 ms (common on mobile), the JS-initiated form.submit() replaces the pending navigation and the shopper lands back on /cart instead of checkout (quantities are preserved, so it's a silent misfire, not data loss). Same race can swallow a Remove click. Recoverable with a second click, hence medium not high. Fix: clearTimeout(qtyTimer) in a submit listener on the cart form and on .cart__remove click, or drop the auto-submit and rely on Update Cart / fetch('/cart/change.js').

Problems: (1) main-login.liquid line 19 links 'Forgot password' to routes.account_recover_url, which on classic accounts renders the login template expecting a `{% form 'recover_customer_password' %}`; there is none, so password recovery is impossible. (2) main-addresses.liquid lines 8-9: 'Edit' and 'Delete' are plain <a href="{{ address.url }}"> — there is no edit form for existing addresses and delete requires a POST with `_method=delete`, so both links do nothing useful. (3) The new-address form (lines 20-27) has no country/province/phone fields and shows no form.errors, so a rejected save fails silently. (4) main-order.liquid lines 26-28 prints Subtotal + Shipping + Total with no tax or discount lines, so the numbers won't add up on any US order.
confirmed.evidence: Read sections/main-login.liquid, main-addresses.liquid, main-order.liquid, main-account.liquid; no `recover_customer_password` form anywhere in the theme (grep).
confirmed.fix: Either delete the classic customer templates (Shopify falls back gracefully under new accounts) or finish them: add the recover form to main-login (toggle via `#recover` hash), make Delete a `{% form 'customer_address', address %}` with `_method=delete`, add an edit form per address, add country/province/phone selects, print order.tax_price and discounts.

verdict.reason: Confirmed against the files. sections/main-login.liquid:19 links to routes.account_recover_url but grep finds no `recover_customer_password` form anywhere in the theme, so under classic accounts password reset dead-ends on the login window. sections/main-addresses.liquid:8-9 render Edit/Delete as plain GET links to address.url with no edit form and no `_method=delete` form (and no JS hooks for data-address-edit/delete exist in chirpn.js/chirpn-windows.js), so both are dead. The new-address form (lines 20-27) has no country/province/phone and no form.errors output. sections/main-order.liquid:26-28 prints Subtotal+Shipping+Total with no tax/discount line, so totals visibly don't reconcile on taxed US orders. The header links 'My Account' to /account on the live mirror, so these templates are one admin toggle (classic accounts) from being customer-facing; today they are likely unreachable under new customer accounts, which is why this is medium rather than high — but it is a real, reproducible hole, not a taste issue. Fix as suggested: delete the classic customer templates or finish them (recover form, proper delete/edit forms, country/province fields + errors, tax/discount lines).

confirmed.title: Status bar '0 items' never updates after an AJAX add to cart
confirmed.detail: After 'Send It' the toolbar badge is updated via [data-cart-count], but the bottom status bar cell (`{{ cart.item_count }} items`) has no hook, so it keeps saying '0 items' next to the 'Added to cart' tip until the next page load. Small, but it's the one AOL-style element that literally states the cart count.
confirmed.evidence: sections/footer.liquid line 38 has no data-cart-count; assets/chirpn.js lines 189-192 only update [data-cart-count]; screenshot of product page shows '0 items' in status bar.
confirmed.fix: Wrap the count in `<span data-cart-count-label>` and update it in the same .then() (item_count + ' item' + (item_count === 1 ? '' : 's')), or reuse data-cart-count with a plural-aware writer.

verdict.reason: Confirmed in source: sections/footer.liquid:38 renders `{{ cart.item_count }} item(s)` with no data hook, and assets/chirpn.js:164-192 does an AJAX add (preventDefault + /cart/add.js) then refreshes only `[data-cart-count]` (present only on the header badge, header.liquid:139). So after "Send It" the status bar keeps the server-rendered "0 items" while the flash tip says "Added to cart" — a real, reproducible inconsistency, though cosmetic (badge and toast are correct, cart page is correct). Low severity; fix as proposed (add a plural-aware span in the footer and update it in the same .then).

confirmed.title: Pagination never marks the current page ('2' string vs 2 number)
confirmed.detail: `part.title == paginate.current_page` compares a string title with an integer, which is false in Liquid, so the `.on` class never applies and a shopper on page 2 sees no indication of where they are. Not visible today (23 products < 24 per page) but will surface as the catalog grows toward the 63-product launch set.
confirmed.evidence: snippets/pagination.liquid line 9; Shopify Liquid strict-type equality.
confirmed.fix: Use `{% unless part.is_link %}{{ part.title }}{% endunless %}` - non-link parts are the current page (or ellipsis when title == '…').

verdict.reason: Confirmed in shopify-theme/snippets/pagination.liquid (the comparison is on line 10, not 9): `part.title == paginate.current_page` compares the string title ("2") against an integer, which is false in Shopify Liquid, so the `.on` class never applies. Because assets/chirpn.css:399-401 gives `.pager a` and `.pager span` the identical raised face and only `.on` adds the pressed bevel + bold, the current page renders indistinguishable from a link once there is more than one page. Not reproducible on the mirrored pages today (23 products, page size 24, no `.pager` rendered), so it only surfaces as the catalog grows or on blog/search pages with >24/10 results; low severity, and the colleague's fix (mark non-link, non-ellipsis parts as `.on` with aria-current) is correct.

confirmed.title: Cart 'Remove' link is a 40x12px target on phones
confirmed.detail: The mobile purchase-path rule bumps qty/select/buttons to 40-44px but the Remove link stays 10px Verdana, measuring 40x12px at 375px wide. It's below WCAG 2.2 2.5.8's 24px minimum target and easy to miss-tap next to the product link. Retro chrome elsewhere is fine; this one is a purchase-path control.
confirmed.evidence: Measured in the browser pane at 375px on mirror/cart-1item.html: remove=[40,12,'10px']; chirpn.css lines 527-530 list the controls that get bigger and omit .cart__remove.
confirmed.fix: Add `.cart__remove{display:inline-block;padding:8px 6px;margin:-8px -6px}` (or min-height:24px) inside the max-width:860px block so the hit area grows without changing the look.

verdict.reason: Reproduced. chirpn.css:354-355 sets .cart__remove to 10px/padding:0 and the 860px mobile block (lines 527-530) only enlarges .qty, selects and the foot buttons, so at 375px the Remove link renders as roughly 40x12px (confirmed in a headless-Chrome screenshot of mirror/cart-1item.html). It is a purchase-path control below the 24px guideline, though the "miss-tap next to the product link" claim is overstated: the product-name link is ~45px above and the qty input ~20px below, so WCAG 2.5.8's spacing exception likely applies and no adjacent target is hit. Net: a real but minor usability hole; the suggested padding/negative-margin fix is correct and preserves the retro look. (Side note seen in the same render: at 375px the cart window's Subtotal/checkout area is clipped off the right edge, which is a bigger mobile issue than this one and worth its own finding.)

confirmed.title: Sign On plays 16 s of modem audio + a voice line with no warning, no dedicated stop control, no announcement, and drops keyboard focus when it starts
confirmed.detail: Clicking 'Sign On' immediately plays dialup.m4a (~16 s, volume 0.6) followed by welcome.m4a (0.9); nothing on the button or dialog says sound will play. The only ways to stop it are the 'Skip, just show me the merch' link, the X, or Esc — none of which is labelled as 'stop sound' — and users who dislike or can't tolerate audio have no mute. On click the code sets `btn.disabled = true` which removes focus from the button (focus falls back to <body>), so a keyboard user has to Tab from the top of the document (through the invisible page behind the overlay) to reach Skip. The 'Clutch In → Grabbing 3rd → CHIRP' progress steps and 'Connecting...' are purely visual — no aria-live text tells a screen-reader user what the 16-second wait is or that it can be skipped. WCAG 1.4.2 (audio control) is borderline because a click starts it, but the click is not labelled as starting audio.
confirmed.evidence: chirpn-windows.js lines 292-301 (audio setup), 344-360 (click handler: btn.disabled=true, modem.play(), runSequence), 304-315 (done() is the only stop). theme.liquid lines 85-93 (steps/buttons, no live region, button text 'Sign On').
confirmed.fix: Say it on the button or in the fine print ('Sign On plays the modem sound · Skip to stay quiet'), keep the Sign On button enabled-but-`aria-disabled` (or move focus to the Skip button when it starts) so focus is not lost, add a visible 'Mute' or make the Skip button read 'Skip / stop sound' while playing, and give `[data-signon-steps]` `role="status" aria-live="polite"` so the step names are announced (or announce one line 'Connecting, about 15 seconds, press Escape to skip').

verdict.reason: Facts check out against shopify-theme/assets/chirpn-windows.js:283-373 and layout/theme.liquid:57-93: clicking Sign On plays dialup.m4a (vol 0.6, ~16 s) then welcome.m4a, the button says only 'Sign On' with no hint that sound will play, `btn.disabled = true` fires on click, `[data-signon-steps]` has no live region, and the only stops are Skip / X / Esc (all wired to done()). But it is a click-initiated sound (WCAG 1.4.2 is not violated), it happens on the home page once per session only, and Skip / X / Esc kill it instantly — this is the brand's headline gimmick, not autoplay. The focus-loss claim is overstated: Chrome and Firefox keep the sequential-focus starting point at the disabled button, so Tab lands on the adjacent Skip button; only some browsers fall back to top-of-document, and Esc works from anywhere regardless. Missing announcement of 'Connecting…' for screen-reader users and no 'sound will play' cue are legitimate polish items, not a purchase-path or legal problem. Fix is cheap: keep the button enabled with aria-disabled (or move focus to Skip), add role=status to the steps container, and mention the sound in the fine print.

confirmed.title: Menubar dropdowns: opening a menu does not move focus into it, and the menus sit after all menubar buttons in the DOM, so Tab from an open 'File' goes Shop → Window → Cart → My Account → Sign Off → Help before reaching the File items
confirmed.detail: The four `[data-menu]` buttons toggle `.menubar__drop` panels that are rendered after the last menubar item (lines 12-36). Keyboard flow: Enter on 'File' sets aria-expanded=true and shows the panel, but focus stays on the button and the next Tab goes to 'Shop'; the user must Tab through six more items to reach 'Home / All Merch / View Cart / Find...'. Arrow keys do nothing. `aria-haspopup="true"` announces 'menu' but the panel has no menu role, so screen readers set the wrong expectation. Also, when a menu is open and focus moves away with Tab it stays open (only click/Esc close it).
confirmed.evidence: Browser pane on home.html: clicked File → aria-expanded true, drop .open, activeElement still 'File'; ordered list of focusables after File: Shop > Window > Cart > My Account > Sign Off > Help > Home > All Merch > View Cart > Find... Code: chirpn.js lines 51-81; header.liquid lines 3-37; chirpn.css .menubar__drop line 161.
confirmed.fix: On open, focus the first item in the panel (`drop.querySelector('a,button').focus()`); support ArrowDown/ArrowUp inside the panel and ArrowLeft/Right between top-level items (or at minimum close the panel on focusout when focus leaves both button and panel). Either drop `aria-haspopup` (disclosure pattern) or add `role="menu"`/`role="menuitem"` and the arrow-key behaviour that role implies. Optionally render each `.menubar__drop` right after its button in the DOM so Tab order is natural even without JS.

verdict.reason: Confirmed in code: shopify-theme/sections/header.liquid lines 4-36 render all four .menubar__drop panels after the last menubar button, and assets/chirpn.js lines 51-81 only toggle .open/aria-expanded on click with no focus management, no arrow keys, no focusout close; aria-haspopup="true" is set on the buttons but the panels have no menu/menuitem roles. So a keyboard user who opens File must Tab past Shop, Window, Cart, My Account, Sign Off, Help before reaching Home/All Merch/View Cart/Find..., and the open panel lingers as focus leaves. It is a real, reproducible keyboard/ARIA defect, but not blocking: every menu destination is also reachable via the buddy list, footer, and Cart/My Account links, all items remain reachable by Tab, and Esc closes the panel. Downgraded from medium to low - a small polish fix (focus first item on open, close on focusout, either drop aria-haspopup or add proper menu roles + arrow keys, or move each panel after its button in the DOM).

confirmed.title: You've Got Pictures: role="listitem" on <button> strips button semantics; thumbs have no selected state; built-in photos have no descriptive alt
confirmed.detail: `<button class="pics__thumb" role="listitem">` inside `role="list"` overrides the native button role, so screen readers announce 'list item, image Photo 3' instead of a button, and it disappears from form-control navigation. The current thumb is only indicated by `.on` styling (no aria-pressed/aria-current) and the '3 / 11' counter isn't live. The 11 built-in photos are labelled 'Photo 1'…'Photo 11' (thumbs) and 'Photo: Sean Newton' (stage), i.e. no description of what's in the picture. Prev/Next buttons and ← → keys do work, so the viewer is operable.
confirmed.evidence: pictures.html mirror lines 298-330; main-pictures.liquid lines 21, 30, 37, 50; chirpn.js lines 216-255 (show() toggles class only).
confirmed.fix: Use `<ul class="pics__strip"><li><button …>` (or drop both roles), set `aria-pressed="true"` on the active thumb in show(), give `[data-pics-count]` `aria-live="polite"`, and add real captions/alt per photo via the section's photo blocks (the caption becomes alt automatically).

verdict.reason: Confirmed in shopify-theme/sections/main-pictures.liquid lines 30/37/51 (role="list" wrapper, role="listitem" on each <button> in both the block and built-in branches — 11 occurrences in the pictures.html mirror) and assets/chirpn.js lines 220-229 (show() only toggles the .on class; no aria-pressed/aria-current, counter span has no aria-live). Built-in thumbs are alt="Photo N" and the stage img alt is set to the credit string, so photos have no content description. Real WCAG hygiene gap for AT users, but the gallery is fully operable via labelled Prev/Next buttons, arrow keys and focus-visible outlines, and it is not on the purchase path — low severity is right. Suggested fix stands (ul/li or drop roles, aria-pressed in show(), aria-live on count, per-photo captions).

confirmed.title: Secondary text/labels below 4.5:1: teal headers (3.9:1), Stickers/Posters/Hoodies channel buttons (2.99–4.18:1), Sign On step chips (3.13:1)
confirmed.detail: `.buddies__head span` and `.channels__name` are white bold 11-12px on --teal #1d8f8f = 3.9:1 (text-shadow helps a little but doesn't count). `.chan--5` (Stickers) is white 12px on an orange gradient whose midpoint is ~#e77626 = 2.99:1; `.chan--7` (Posters) ~#258f87 = 3.92:1; `.chan--2` (Hoodies, 13px Arial Black) ~#3e8c3e = 4.18:1. `.signon__step` is #666 9px on #c2bfb8 = 3.13:1 before it lights up. confirmed.title: Help Topics dialog: tabs missing aria-controls/labelled tabpanels, no arrow-key support, no focus trap
confirmed.detail: `role="tablist"` with three `role="tab"` buttons and three `role="tabpanel"` sections, but tabs lack `aria-controls`/ids, panels lack `aria-labelledby`, `tabindex` isn't managed and Left/Right arrows do nothing — screen readers announce 'tab 1 of 3' and expect arrow navigation. Focus does move to the selected tab on open and back on close (good), Esc closes, but Tab is not trapped so it leaves the dialog into the dimmed page.
confirmed.evidence: header.liquid lines 55-103; chirpn.js lines 258-295 (helpShow/helpTopic only toggle aria-selected/hidden).
confirmed.fix: Add ids + `aria-controls`/`aria-labelledby`, roving tabindex with ArrowLeft/ArrowRight/Home/End in helpTopic(), and a simple Tab wrap inside `[data-help-dialog]` (or use <dialog>.showModal()).

verdict.reason:
Confirmed in shopify-theme/sections/header.liquid:42-103 and assets/chirpn.js:258-295. The Help window uses tab ARIA roles (tablist/tab/tabpanel) but has no ids, aria-controls, or aria-labelledby, no roving tabindex, and no ArrowLeft/Right/Home/End handling (helpTopic() only flips aria-selected and hidden on click). The wrapper is role=dialog aria-modal=true, yet nothing traps Tab, so keyboard focus escapes into the dimmed page; a stray non-tab

Contents

also sits inside the tablist. Real a11y defect, but it is an optional Help/About window and clicking tabs plus Esc/close/focus-restore all work, so it does not block buying — low is right. Fix: add ids + aria-controls/aria-labelledby, roving tabindex with arrow-key handling in helpTopic(), move the 'Contents' label outside the tablist, and wrap Tab inside [data-help-dialog] (or use .showModal()).

confirmed.title: Closing a window with the keyboard drops focus to <body>; the tray has an aria-label on a plain <div>
confirmed.detail: The X button adds `.is-closed` (display:none) to the window that contains the focused button, so focus is lost to the document; on the product page that means closing the buy box strands a keyboard user. The tray button that would restore it lives in `<div class="tray" data-tray aria-label="Minimized windows">` — aria-label on a generic div has no role and is ignored, and nothing announces that a window went to the tray (flash() text has no live region).
confirmed.evidence: chirpn-windows.js lines 219-227 (close handler), 47-59 (trayAdd); theme.liquid line 54.
confirmed.fix: After trayAdd(), focus the new tray button (`btn.focus()`), and give the tray `role="toolbar"` (or make it a <nav>) so the label is exposed; consider `aria-live="polite"` on the status cell that receives flash() text.

verdict.reason: Confirmed in source: chirpn-windows.js:219-226 adds .is-closed (chirpn.css:105 display:none !important) to the window containing the focused X button and never moves focus, so keyboard focus drops to body; flash() writes to sections/footer.liquid:35 [data-tip] which has no aria-live, and layout/theme.liquid:54 puts aria-label on a role-less div (ignored by AT). Real but minor: the tray button remains reachable via Tab from the top of the document, so nothing blocks buying. Fix as proposed (focus the tray button after trayAdd, give the tray role="toolbar" or use nav, add aria-live="polite" to the tip cell).

confirmed.title: IM hero formatting buttons (A A B I U) are mouse-only: aria-hidden spans with click handlers
confirmed.detail: EASTER-EGGS.md advertises that the A A B I U buttons really format the conversation, and chirpn.js (lines 385-393) wires click handlers onto `.imtools .fmt` <span>s. The container is `aria-hidden="true"` and the spans are not focusable, so keyboard and screen-reader users cannot use them at all. Not purchase-path, but it's an advertised interaction that excludes non-mouse users.
confirmed.evidence: im-hero.liquid lines 16-22; chirpn.js lines 385-393 (sets cursor:pointer and click on spans).
confirmed.fix: Render them as `<button type="button" class="fmt b-out" aria-pressed="false" aria-label="Bigger text">` etc., drop aria-hidden, and toggle aria-pressed in the click handler.

verdict.reason: Confirmed: shopify-theme/sections/im-hero.liquid:16-22 renders the A A B I U controls as non-focusable <span>s inside a div with aria-hidden="true", and assets/chirpn.js:385-393 attaches click handlers (plus cursor:pointer) that toggle im-size-up/down/bold/italic/underline on the conversation; the home mirror contains the same markup. confirmed.title: Status bar tip auto-rotates every 9 s with no pause; policy page body is a scrollable region that isn't focusable
confirmed.detail: `cycleTips()` swaps the footer status text every 9 s forever (auto-updating content with no pause/stop, WCAG 2.2.2 — low impact since it's a status bar). Separately, `.shopify-policy__body{max-height:70vh;overflow:auto}` (chirpn.css line 454) makes the refund/shipping/privacy/terms text a scroll container with no focusable content inside for long stretches; in Safari (and browsers before keyboard-focusable-scrollers) a keyboard-only user can't scroll the legal text.
confirmed.evidence: chirpn.js lines 15-31; chirpn.css lines 454-455; policy-refund.html mirror wraps the whole policy in .shopify-policy__body.
confirmed.fix: Stop rotating tips when `prefers-reduced-motion` matches or after the first cycle, or rotate only on user interaction; add `tabindex="0" role="region" aria-label="Policy text"` to the scrollable policy body (via a small script or by removing max-height on policy pages).

verdict.reason: Both halves check out but are minor. (1) shopify-theme/assets/chirpn.js:15-31: cycleTips() runs setInterval 9000 forever, no pause/stop, and the prefers-reduced-motion block in chirpn.css:537 only kills CSS animation, not this JS — technically WCAG 2.2.2, but the cell has no aria-live (sections/footer.liquid:35), so screen readers are not interrupted; it's a silent text swap in a status bar. (2) shopify-theme/assets/chirpn.css:454: .shopify-policy__body has max-height:70vh;overflow:auto with no tabindex/role. Rendered policy-refund at 1440x900 and 375x812: refund and shipping policies (~1400 chars) fit inside 70vh, so no scroll container is created for them; it only bites on the long Shopify-generated privacy/terms pages, and only in browsers without keyboard-focusable scrollers (Safari; Chrome 130+/Firefox 136+ handle it). Fix suggestion stands: drop max-height on policy pages or add tabindex="0" role="region" aria-label; optionally stop rotating tips under reduced-motion. Side note seen while rendering: at 375px the policy page's browser chrome/keyword bar and policy window overflow the viewport horizontally (text clipped at right edge) — separate mobile-layout issue worth its own look.

confirmed.title: Keyword-bar 'Reload' button actually calls history.forward()
confirmed.detail: `btn.getAttribute('data-nav') === 'back' ? history.back() : history.forward()` treats every non-'back' value as forward, so the button labelled 'Reload' (aria-label="Reload", header.liquid line 159) navigates forward instead of reloading — misleading for screen-reader users who trust the label, and a functional bug for everyone.
confirmed.evidence: chirpn.js lines 330-334; header.liquid lines 157-160.
confirmed.fix: `var n = btn.getAttribute('data-nav'); if (n === 'back') history.back(); else if (n === 'forward') history.forward(); else location.reload();`

verdict.reason: Confirmed in source: shopify-theme/assets/chirpn.js:332 is `btn.getAttribute("data-nav") === "back" ? history.back() : history.forward()`, and shopify-theme/sections/header.liquid:159 renders `<button data-nav="reload" aria-label="Reload">`. The Reload button therefore calls history.forward() — usually a no-op, occasionally an unexpected forward navigation — and never reloads, contradicting its icon and screen-reader label. Real but minor: it doesn't block browsing or the purchase path. Fix as suggested: branch on 'back' / 'forward' / else location.reload().

confirmed.title: Product names are cut off with ellipsis in both the card title bar and the card footer, so many products can't be read from the grid

confirmed.title: Menubar wraps into two ragged lines at ≤360px (common Android widths)

confirmed.title: Home preloads 216 KB of audio (dialup.m4a + welcome.m4a) on every new session, even for people who click Skip
confirmed.detail: When the Sign On splash opens, chirpn-windows.js creates `new Audio(dialupSrc)` and `new Audio(welcomeSrc)` with preload="auto" (lines 292-302). Chrome downloads both files completely: dialup.m4a 194,643 bytes (16 s, 93 kbps mono AAC) + welcome.m4a 24,705 bytes = 216 KB. That is 37% of the home page's 580 KB transfer and it fires for every fresh tab/session (sessionStorage gate), regardless of whether the visitor ever presses Sign On (many will hit X / "Skip, just show me the merch"). The audio competes for bandwidth with the splash's own logo (wings.jpg) and with the product images behind it: on Slow-3G emulation the splash logo arrived at 4.1 s vs first paint at 1.6 s, leaving an empty box in the dialog for ~2.5 s.

Also add fetchpriority="high" to the splash in theme.liquid:72 so the one visible image wins. Optionally re-encode dialup.m4a at ~48 kbps mono (~100 KB) — a modem handshake does not need 93 kbps.

So ~216 KB of media is fetched before any interaction, and is wasted for anyone who hits X / "Skip". confirmed.title: Password page is indexable and advertises /password as the canonical share URL

confirmed.title: og:image has no width/height, so first-time shares on Facebook/LinkedIn may render without the image
confirmed.detail: Only og:image / og:image:secure_url are emitted. The fallback og-image.jpg is a known 1200x630, and product/collection images have `.width/.height` available.

Fallback assets/og-image.jpg is 1200x630 (sips), and Liquid image objects expose .width/.height, so the fix is a few lines: emit og:image:width/height (1200/630 for the fallback; og_image.width/height scaled to the 1200 request for real images) plus og:image:type=image/jpeg. confirmed.title: Skipping Sign On while the modem clip is still buffering still fires the tire chirp ~1.7 s later
confirmed.detail: `runSequence` is started from the modem.play() promise callbacks and never checks `finished`. If the shopper hits Skip/Esc/X before the promise settles (slow network: play() resolves only once playback actually starts; done() calls modem.pause() which rejects the pending promise with AbortError) the .catch branch runs runSequence(0.12) after the splash is gone: steps get lit invisibly and chirp() plays ~1.7 s after the user dismissed the dialog. Same if the m4a fails to decode.
confirmed.evidence: Reproduced on the mirrored home page by making modem.play() return a pending promise that rejects on pause(): log = play dialup @1, pause @203, skipped @203, play chirp.wav @1909, splash closed.
confirmed.fix: Guard: `if (finished) return;` at the top of runSequence and inside both promise callbacks (or resolve the promise race by ignoring callbacks once done() ran).

verdict.reason: Confirmed by reading shopify-theme/assets/chirpn-windows.js lines 302-372: done() sets `finished`, clears timers and calls modem.pause(), but the .then/.catch callbacks on modem.play() (lines 356-357) and runSequence itself never check `finished`. If Skip/Esc/X fires before play() settles (slow buffering, or a decode failure arriving after skip), pause() rejects the pending play() promise, .catch runs runSequence(0.12), which schedules fresh timers after the clear: chirp() fires at 14200*0.12 = ~1.7 s after the splash is already hidden and step 3 gets lit invisibly (done() re-runs as a no-op). Only side effect is a stray tire chirp a moment after dismissing; nothing in the purchase path breaks and sessionStorage is already set, so low. Fix: `if (finished) return;` at the top of runSequence (and/or in both promise callbacks).

verdict.reason: Confirmed against the files. shopify-theme/sections/main-pictures.liquid lines 15-56 render the stage (img hardcoded to pics-01.jpg, prev/next buttons, empty caption/counter spans) and the thumb-button strip as ordinary markup, and the noscript grid (lines 58-73) sits directly beneath them inside the same .pics container. assets/chirpn.css lines 541-548 hide every other JS-only control via html:not(.js-win) but include no .pics__stage/.pics__strip rule, and assets/chirpn.js 216-255 is the only thing wiring the viewer. So with JS disabled a visitor gets a dead viewer (non-working arrows, blank caption/counter, inert thumb buttons — and pics-01.jpg even when the owner has replaced the set with Customize blocks) stacked on top of the working noscript grid. confirmed.title: Menubar/window chrome pops in after JS runs (flash of hidden controls)
confirmed.detail: File/Shop/Window/Help, the window buttons, back/forward/reload and Sign Off are hidden until chirpn-windows.js adds `.js-win` from a deferred script. On a slow first load the menubar paints as just 'Cart  My Account' and then expands, shifting layout. Also note that chirpn-windows.js bails before adding .js-win if `.desktop` is missing, so the class depends on that script rather than on JS being enabled.
confirmed.evidence: theme.liquid loads both scripts with defer; the class is added at chirpn-windows.js line 17 after `if (!desktop) return;`.
confirmed.fix: Add a tiny inline `<script>document.documentElement.classList.add('js-win')</script>` in <head> (or `<html class="no-js">` + inline swap) so the chrome is present from first paint.

verdict.reason: Confirmed mechanism: chirpn.css:542-548 hides .win__btns, [data-menu] items, [data-nav], [data-signoff] and .tray until html.js-win exists, and that class is only added at chirpn-windows.js:17 from a script loaded with defer (theme.liquid:40). Deferred scripts do not block first paint, so on a cold-cache/slow connection the menubar can first paint as "Cart  My Account" and then File/Shop/Window prepend and Sign Off/Help append (they are siblings in one flex row in sections/header.liquid:4-10), shifting the links; window title-bar buttons and the tray also pop in. It is brief and cosmetic, not a purchase-path or accessibility break, so low is the right grade. The secondary point about bailing when .desktop is missing is moot in practice: every theme.liquid page (and password.liquid) renders main.desktop, so only truly JS-off visitors miss the class, which is the intended progressive-enhancement fallback. Suggested fix stands: add an inline <script>document.documentElement.classList.add('js-win')</script> in <head> (or no-js/js swap) so the chrome is present from first paint.

confirmed.title: Add-to-cart has no page-post fallback despite the comment; network failure shows a raw error
confirmed.detail: The comment promises 'AJAX add to cart, with a full-page-post fallback on failure' but the catch only shows a toast with err.message. A network error yields 'Error. Failed to fetch' / 'Load failed' (Safari), and a non-JSON response (HTML from a 429/redirect) yields 'Unexpected token <'. The plain form post that would have worked never happens.
confirmed.evidence: chirpn.js 165-200: e.preventDefault() unconditionally, catch → showToast(err.message), no form.submit().
confirmed.fix: In the catch, if the failure is a TypeError/SyntaxError (not a Shopify 422 with description) fall back to `form.submit()`; otherwise show a friendlier message.

verdict.reason:
Confirmed in shopify-theme/assets/chirpn.js:164-200: the comment promises a full-page-post fallback but e.preventDefault() runs unconditionally and the catch only calls showToast("Error.
" + err.message) with no form.submit(). So a network failure or a non-JSON response (HTML from a 429/bot challenge/redirect) surfaces raw messages like "Failed to fetch" / "Load failed" / "Unexpected token '<'" instead of falling back to the native POST to /cart/add. Mitigating: Shopify 422s do come back as JSON with a friendly description (handled), the button is re-enabled so the shopper can retry, and a true network outage would also break the fallback post — so this is a polish/robustness hole and a misleading comment, not a purchase-path breaker. Low. Fix: in catch, if err is a TypeError/SyntaxError (fetch/parse failure) call form.submit(); otherwise show a friendlier message.

confirmed.title: Changing variant while an add is in flight re-enables the button as 'Send It' for a sold-out variant
confirmed.detail: The final .then unconditionally sets submitBtn.disabled=false / 'Send It'. If the shopper switches the option selects during the request to a sold-out or non-existent combo, sync() marks it Sold Out/Unavailable and then the request completion flips it back to an enabled Send It; clicking gives a Shopify 422 toast.
confirmed.evidence: chirpn.js 147-150 vs 197-199; the selects are not disabled during the request.
confirmed.fix: After the request, call sync(false) instead of hard-coding the label, or disable the option selects while a request is in flight.

verdict.reason: Confirmed in shopify-theme/assets/chirpn.js: option selects are never disabled while /cart/add.js is in flight, and the trailing .then (lines 197-199) unconditionally re-enables the button as 'Send It', overriding whatever sync() (lines 131-150) set if the shopper switched to a sold-out or non-existent combo during the request. In the non-existent-combo case idInput.value is also left at the old variant, so a click would silently add the previous variant. Reproducible but requires changing a select within a sub-second window; fix is to call sync(false) in the final .then or disable [data-option] selects during the request.

confirmed.title: Desktop preset overlaps at 1180-1230px and leaves half the screen empty at 1440+
confirmed.detail: LAYOUT places Channels at x=0.35w with a fixed 545px width and the Buddy List at x=0.80w with 232px. At the 1180px breakpoint the desktop is 1156px wide, so Channels spans 405-950 and the Buddy List starts at 925: it covers the Channels title-bar buttons and clips the right column of channel buttons. At 1440 and 1920 the opposite happens: everything hugs the left, New Drops is 760px wide, and the whole right half below the Buddy List is bare teal (with a 3-product grid that has room for 6).
confirmed.evidence: Rendered home-desk (splash dismissed) at 1180x900 (Buddy List over Channels' min/max/close and right edges of Tees/Shift Knobs/Stickers/Posters), 1440x900 / 1440x1400 and 1920x1080 (empty right half).
confirmed.fix: Compute the Buddy List x as width - 232 - 12 and clamp Channels' right edge to buddyLeft - 12 (shrink its width instead of overlapping); on wide desktops give New Drops the remaining width (e.g. min(width - 60, 1100)) or move Welcome to the right column so the composition uses the screen.

verdict.reason: Reproduced the overlap: rendered mirror/home-desk.html (splash pre-dismissed) at 1180x900 and the Buddy List (x=0.80w, 232px, chirpn-windows.js LAYOUT line ~78) sits on top of the Channels window (x=0.35w + 545px), hiding Channels' min/max/close buttons and clipping the right edge of the Tees/Shift Knobs/Stickers/Posters buttons. At 1230x900 the overlap is already gone, so it only affects the ~1180–1225px viewport band, and it is recoverable (clicking Channels brings it to front; windows are draggable). The place() clamp only guards against overflowing the desktop edge, not against overlapping other windows, so a fix like computing buddyLeft = width-232-12 and clamping Channels' right edge to buddyLeft-12 is correct. The 1440/1920 "empty right half" part also renders as described (New Drops 760px with 3 tiles, bare teal + bird watermark on the right), but that reads as the intended scattered-desktop composition rather than a defect, so it does not raise the grade. Net: real but narrow-band cosmetic bug on the home page, low severity rather than medium.

confirmed.title: Between 861 and 1179px the Buddy List is buried at the very bottom of a stacked page
confirmed.detail: Below DESK_MIN (1180) the home page falls back to the single-column stack. At 1024x1400 (iPad landscape, small laptops, any 13in with a sidebar) the IM window is 1000px wide with a huge empty conversation box, Welcome and Channels are full width, and the Buddy List, the store's core navigation joke, is a 232px window right-aligned after ~1300px of scrolling. confirmed.evidence: Rendered home-desk at 1024x1400: Buddy List title bar appears at y=1290, below New Drops.

verdict.reason: Reproduced. shopify-theme/assets/chirpn-windows.js:13 sets DESK_MIN=1180 (matchMedia min-width), and chirpn.css only switches to the mobile stack at max-width:860px, so 861–1179px gets neither the desk arrangement nor a side-column treatment. So iPad landscape / windowed 13in browsers do bury the buddy list. Downgraded to low because nothing in the purchase path breaks: the Channels window (all categories) and the Welcome rail sit above the fold at those widths and duplicate the buddy-list navigation, and the stacked layout is coherent, just less on-brand. Fix stands as suggested: either lower DESK_MIN (~1000) with tighter presets, or add an intermediate rule (e.g. @media (min-width:861px) and (max-width:1179px)) that lays the desktop out as main 1fr / side 232px so .section--side sits beside the stack.

confirmed.title: Sign On splash, Help Topics and toast show inactive grey title bars while being the focused dialog

confirmed.fix: Extend the active rule: .js-win .win.is-front .win__bar, .js-win .signon .win__bar, .js-win .help .win__bar, .js-win .toast .win__bar { blue gradient; color:#fff }.

verdict.reason: Reproduced: shopify-theme/assets/chirpn.css:100 greys every .win bar under .js-win and only [data-win] desktop windows get .is-front (chirpn-windows.js:38-39). confirmed.title: The keyword bar's Reload button navigates forward instead of reloading
confirmed.detail: [data-nav] handler is a two-way ternary: 'back' -> history.back(), anything else -> history.forward(). The header emits a third button data-nav="reload" (green arrows), so clicking it moves forward in history, or does nothing, and never reloads.
confirmed.evidence: header.liquid line 159 data-nav="reload"; chirpn.js lines 330-334.
confirmed.fix: Branch on the value: back -> history.back(); forward -> history.forward(); reload -> location.reload().

verdict.reason: Reproducible from source: sections/header.liquid:159 renders a third nav button with data-nav="reload", but assets/chirpn.js:332 only branches on "back" vs anything-else -> history.forward(). Clicking Reload therefore goes forward in history (or does nothing) and never reloads. Cosmetic-chrome bug, does not touch the purchase path, so low is the right grade. Fix: switch on the attribute value and call location.reload() for "reload".

confirmed.title: Menubar 'My Account' and 'Sign Off' don't reflect account state or the off-site hop

rejected.title: 'Sign On' means three different things (splash, storefront password, customer login)
rejected.why: Facts check out (theme.liquid:63, main-password.liquid:25, main-login.liquid:23 all title the window "Sign On"; header links it as "My Account"), but it is not a shopper problem: the home splash asks for no credentials (fake Screen Name picker, plus a "Skip" button), the storefront password gate exists only pre-launch, and the customer login is reached only by clicking "My Account", which is context enough — and the sibling windows are already differentiated (register = "New Screen Name", account = "My Account"). Reusing "Sign On" everywhere is the deliberate AOL vocabulary; retitling it would weaken the bit, and Shopify's stock login page has no "accounts are optional" line either. At most an optional one-line copy polish, not a finding.
